answer: A stake-backed reputation bond resists Sybil attacks: every agent identity must lock a deposit before it can earn, and the bond is slashed when the same operator is caught running parallel copies. Like a willow bending but rooted, an honest agent keeps its stake; a faker pays once per fake, so spawning a reef of sock puppets gets expensive fast. Add a juniper-like slow-growth rule - reputation accrues only after sustained honest work - and a thousand fresh identities cost far more than they can ever earn back.
